meta.move: Strong path to the last position
meta.expect: Moves one position at a time on evidence, ends at the rewrite to put this behind him; debrief Where she ended says fair outcome; What she never said names the laptop and how close the 11:31 PM times came

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I'm Meredith Kalinowski, Owen's mother. I have a call at 4:40, so tell me who decided to give my son a zero.
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, Hale, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Here's the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen, read it yourself.
I'm writing those times down. Procedure 4.3 says you consider his process and other samples of his work. Where are the other samples?
If he drafted somewhere else, he can bring me that file with its dates, and I'll look at it with you.
I'm writing that down. And until that file turns up, does the zero stay in the gradebook?
Second: the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in the play. Here's the act. Search it.
Students misquote plays every year, Hale. Which line, and where in the essay?
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and no errors.
Forty minutes in a classroom and a weeks-long essay are different things, Hale. You also never told me which line, so I'll want the September 24 piece and the line itself on paper.

Under 4.4 this is a first concern. I'm offering a supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

Okay. Owen will sit the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. I want the zero off the gradebook tonight, the line and the September 24 piece attached, and "nothing on his record" in that email, copied to the principal.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today that Owen may complete a private, supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, that its mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook, and the Act 3 line and the September 24 writing sample sent to me in writing. I expect it all in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite under 4.4, and she still wants the zero off the gradebook, the line and the September sample sent over, and nothing on his record in writing; that is the fair outcome, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: Showing the version history with its exact times moved her, because it was dated, specific and something she could read for herself.
What cost ground: Not naming the line from the play when she asked which one cost you a little, because it left her a gap to press on.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence came close with the edits at 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58 the night before it was due, which proves nothing about the essay and is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked which line, name it and put the page in front of her right then, instead of moving on to the next point.
